Understood: fuel = butane. NASA has no tests anywhere in that range for this scenario: unknown. How pressure_kpa acts according to the models: · methanol droplets, at 0.7 atm instead of 1 atm: no clear effect (×0.54, 95 %: 0.1–2.34). · n-heptane droplets, at 0.7 atm instead of 1 atm: no clear effect (×0.54, 95 %: 0.1–2.34). · normal gas flames, +1 bar: helps it go out (×2.28, 95 %: 1.21–4.49). · inverse gas flames (O2 = burner jet, not the cabin air), +1 bar: no clear effect (×1.32, 95 %: 0.96–2.37). Where it was tested: Heptane droplets: pressure_kpa 70.394-102.845 (O2 0.13-0.30), 78 clean tests; Methanol droplets: pressure_kpa 70.1674-103.205 (O2 0.12-0.34), 128 clean tests. Gas flames: the ratio is how much faster the flame goes out by itself (hazard ratio); inverse flames have moderate confidence Droplets: 2-3 atm has only 7 near-identical tests and is shown as evidence only (DD-024)
